title: TDS on Salary: Employer's Calculation Under the New Act
description: From April 1st, 2026, TDS on salary is governed by the new Income Tax Act 2025, replacing the 1961 Act. Your employer deducts Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) fro.

faq.q: What is the new Income Tax Act 2025?
faq.a: The Income Tax Act 2025 is a new legislation effective from April 1st, 2026, which replaces the long-standing Income Tax Act 1961. It governs all aspects of income tax, including TDS on salary, with updated forms and section numbers, though tax rates and slabs remain unchanged.

faq.q: How does the new Act affect my TDS calculation?
faq.a: While the tax rates and slabs for individuals remain the same, the new Act introduces changes to the specific forms and section numbers used for claiming exemptions and deductions. This means the procedural aspects of how your employer calculates and reports TDS have been updated.

faq.q: What if I have multiple employers in a financial year?
faq.a: If you switch jobs, your new employer will consider your income from the previous employer and the TDS already deducted. You must provide Form 16 from your previous employer to your new employer to ensure accurate TDS calculation and avoid over-deduction.

faq.q: Can my employer deduct more TDS than required?
faq.a: Yes, if you do not submit your investment declarations or proofs on time, your employer might deduct higher TDS as they won't consider your eligible deductions. You can claim a refund for any excess TDS when filing your income tax return.

faq.q: What is Form 16 and why is it important?
faq.a: Form 16 is a certificate issued by your employer detailing the salary paid to you and the TDS deducted and deposited on your behalf. It's a crucial document for filing your income tax return as it summarises your income and tax payments.

faq.q: How can I ensure my employer deducts the correct TDS?
faq.a: The most effective way is to accurately declare all your planned investments and expenses through Form 12BB at the start of the financial year and submit actual proofs of these investments and expenses periodically or by the deadlines set by your employer.

faq.q: What if I forget to submit investment proofs?
faq.a: If you miss the deadline for submitting investment proofs, your employer will likely not consider those deductions, leading to higher TDS. You can still claim these deductions when you file your income tax return directly with the Income Tax Department.

fact_check.summary: The article contains several inaccuracies regarding the new Income Tax Act 2025, particularly concerning tax rates, standard deduction, HRA exemption, and the availability of Section 80CCD(1B) deduction under the new regime. While the effective date and replacement of the 1961 Act are correct, the details about the new tax regime's provisions are largely incorrect.
